route: Work permit (Labor Law, art. 33; Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development)

permit.applies: The employer: after the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development approves the recruitment, it obtains the work permit for the worker and bears its fees and the residence fees (Labor Law arts. 32, 33, 40).
permit.first: The Ministry's approval to recruit (Labor Law art. 32).
permit.eligibility: The worker entered the country legally and is authorised to work; holds skills or qualifications the country needs that no citizen holds, or too few, or is in a category of ordinary worker it needs; and is under contract with an employer and working for it (Labor Law art. 33).

sources.title: Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Saudi Arabia), Visa platform (منصة التأشيرات), front page
Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development, 'Employment of Non-Saudis' (Labor Law arts. 32-40)
sources.said: Article 32: Recruitment for the purpose of employment shall not be permitted except after the approval of the Ministry. Article 33: Non-Saudis may not practice any work, nor shall they be permitted to do so, except after obtaining a work permit from the Ministry according to the form prepared for this purpose. The following conditions shall be required for granting the license: The worker must have entered the country legally and be authorized to work. The worker must possess the professional competencies or academic qualifications that the country needs, and there are no citizens who possess them, or the number of citizens who possess them is insufficient to meet the need, or the worker must be from the category of ordinary workers that the country needs. The worker must be under contract with and the responsibility of an employer. ... Article 34: The work permit referred to herein shall not substitute for any permit or license required by another authority to practice the work or profession. ... Article 37: The employment contract for a non-Saudi worker must be written and of a fixed term. If the contract does not specify its duration, it is considered to be one year starting from the worker's actual commencement date. ... Article 40: The employer shall bear the costs of recruiting the foreign worker, the residence and work permit fees and their renewals, along with any penalties resulting from delays in such renewals, the fees for changing the profession, exit and re-entry fees, and the cost of the worker’s return ticket to their home country after the termination of the relationship between the two parties.

note: Saudi Arabia: SLATE's layer 3 held it blocked (its register's R-1545, an id SLATE later removed) when this file was written on 2026-11-01, and what a foreign performer must hold couldn't be read from the authorities then; this rebuild's layer 3 holds the route found (papers.work.SA, R-5080). Closing retry 2026-11-01: the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development’s page on the employment of non-Saudis (read) gives the route, the Labor Law’s work permit, needed by every non-Saudi; who files it, its fees, time and term remain unread. Read again 2026-11-04: the Ministry's page at its old address now redirects to its 'Employment of Non-Saudis' page, which reproduces the Labor Law's arts. 32-40: who applies, what comes first and the criteria. The fees, time and term aren't in those articles (the contract, not the permit, defaults to one year, art. 37), and the work permit doesn't replace another authority's licence (art. 34): for screen work the Film Commission's or the General Entertainment Authority's, neither read.
